newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat harvest surges to 67 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat harvest surges to 67 percent complete.

text.p: The Kansas wheat harvest surged ahead during the week ended Sunday, reaching 67 percent complete, the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
"Drier conditions in many areas allowed harvest to move ahead of 63 percent and just below last year's 74 percent," the update said.
The state's wheat crop was rated 87 percent good or excellent, up from 75 percent a week earlier.
Corn was 23 percent silked, ahead of 18 percent last year and the average of 17 percent.
Sorghum and soybean planting were virtually complete, the report said. Sorghum condition was reported as 83 percent good to excellent, against 85 percent at that level last week.

Soybean blooming was 21 percent complete, ahead of 10 percent last year but behind average of 25 percent. Eighty-one percent of soybeans were in good to excellent condition, down slightly from 84 percent at that level a week ago.
Pasture condition was rated 82 percent good or excellent, up from 80 percent a week earlier.
Topsoil moisture was five percent surplus, 73 percent adequate, 20 percent short and two percent very short.
